crime: Every evening at dusk, a girl sat at the upper railing and wrote in her notebook how her day had felt, while {WITCH_NAME} sat on the floor beside her. One evening the girl read her pages back and laughed. "Half this sadness is yours." From now on, she said, she wanted to write alone. "I'll come find you after."
On a birthday when she was small, {WITCH_NAME} had hidden in the wardrobe, biting her lip until dark. They had called off the game and eaten the cake without her.
So she waited just inside the dark doorway of the library to be found, biting her lip raw.
At the railing, the girl felt that waiting as her own and wrote: "I'm so tired of waiting in the dark. I want it over." Below it she added: "I've bitten my lip raw without noticing."
The courtyard went dark. The girl stayed at the railing, humming, and never once looked toward the doorway.
{WITCH_NAME} took her by the ankles and tipped her over the railing, head first onto the path below. She left the notebook lying open at that page and slipped back into the dark library.
The prisoners read the page as the girl's farewell. She had gone over by herself.

Then one prisoner read that last line and looked at the dead girl's mouth. Her lips were unbroken. The prisoner looked up at {WITCH_NAME}, whose lower lip was bitten raw. In the trial court, that prisoner understood: the page was {WITCH_NAME}'s waiting, felt from a few steps away.
fields.epitaph: She was found at last, by her own heart in another girl's hand.
fields.epithet: Still Hiding After the Game Is Over
execution: The execution stand raises an iron wardrobe around her. Chains hold her upright, and the doors shut. Then the back wall moves in and presses her flat against the closed doors. The spectators feel the wall crushing them too; they clutch their own chests and gasp in step with her. The gasping stops. The wardrobe doors swing open on her, slumped still in her chains, and the spectators breathe again all at once.

magic.name: Fellow Feeling
magic.text: Whatever she feels, the people near her feel too, as if it were their own.
